problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ b & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix of the quadratic form $Q(x)=2{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2}\,$ is given above. What is the value of $a+b?$

feedback.problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & b \\ b & c\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix of the quadratic form $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-2{x}_{2}^{2}\,$ is given above. What is the value of $b+c?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the matrix of the quadratic form must be symmetric, we rewrite our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =3{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-2{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =3{x}_{1}^{2}+1{x}_{1}{x}_{2} \\  & +\,1{x}_{2}{x}_{1}+(-2){x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that to get a symmetric matrix, we must split the coefficient of $2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}$ between the entries 

$$
{a}_{12}={a}_{21}=\frac{2}{2}=1
$$

of our matrix. So, the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $b=1$ and $c=-2.$ Finally, 

$$
b+c=1-2=-1.
$$
